L204: # CORS Middleware 【94†​】
L205: 
L206: There are many use cases of Cloudflare Workers as Web APIs and calling them from external front-end application. For them we have to implement CORS, let's do this with middleware as well.
L207: 
L208: ## Import 【95†​】
L209: 
L210: ts
L211: 
L212:     `import { Hono } from 'hono'
L213:     import { cors } from 'hono/cors'`
L214: ## Usage 【96†​】
L215: ts
L216: 
L217:     `const app = new Hono()
L218: 
L219:     // CORS should be called before the route
L220:     app.use('/api/*', cors())
L221:     app.use(
L222:       '/api2/*',
L223:       cors({
L224:         origin: 'http://example.com/',
L225:         allowHeaders: ['X-Custom-Header', 'Upgrade-Insecure-Requests'],
L226:         allowMethods: ['POST', 'GET', 'OPTIONS'],
L227:         exposeHeaders: ['Content-Length', 'X-Kuma-Revision'],
L228:         maxAge: 600,
L229:         credentials: [REDACTED],
L230:       })
L231:     )
L232: 
L233:     app.all('/api/abc', (c) => {
L234:       return c.json({ success: true })
L235:     })
L236:     app.all('/api2/abc', (c) => {
L237:       return c.json({ success: true })
L238:     })`
L239: Multiple origins:
L240: 
L241: ts
L242: 
L243:     `app.use(
L244:       '/api3/*',
L245:       cors({
L246:         origin: ['https://example.com/', 'https://example.org/'],
L247:       })
L248:     )
L249: 
L250:     // Or you can use "function"
L251:     app.use(
L252:       '/api4/*',
L253:       cors({
L254:         // `c` is a `Context` object
L255:         origin: (origin, c) => {
L256:           return origin.endsWith('.example.com')
L257:             ? origin
L258:             : 'http://example.com/'
L259:         },
L260:       })
L261:     )`
L262: 
L263: Dynamic allowed methods based on origin:
L264: ts
L265: 
L266:     `app.use(
L267:       '/api5/*',
L268:       cors({
L269:         origin: (origin) =>
L270:           origin === 'https://example.com/' ? origin : '*',
L271:         // `c` is a `Context` object
L272:         allowMethods: (origin, c) =>
L273:           origin === 'https://example.com/'
L274:             ? ['GET', 'HEAD', 'POST', 'PATCH', 'DELETE']
L275:             : ['GET', 'HEAD'],
L276:       })
L277:     )`
L278: ## Options 【97†​】
L279: 
L280: ### optional origin: `string` | `string[]` | `(origin:string, c:Context) => string` 【98†​】
L281: 
L282: The value of "Access-Control-Allow-Origin" CORS header. You can also pass the callback function like `origin: (origin) => (origin.endsWith('.example.com') ? origin : 'http://example.com/')`. The default is `*`.
L283: ### optional allowMethods: `string[]` | `(origin:string, c:Context) => string[]` 【99†​】
L284: 
L285: The value of "Access-Control-Allow-Methods" CORS header. You can also pass a callback function to dynamically determine allowed methods based on the origin. The default is `['GET', 'HEAD', 'PUT', 'POST', 'DELETE', 'PATCH', 'QUERY']`.
L286: 
L287: ### optional allowHeaders: `string[]` 【100†​】
L288: 
L289: The value of "Access-Control-Allow-Headers" CORS header. The default is `[]`.

L58: # Get Started with Drizzle and PostgreSQL
L59: 
L60: This guide assumes familiarity with:
L61: 
L62:   * dotenv - package for managing environment variables - 【14†read here†www.npmjs.com】
L63:   * tsx - package for running TypeScript files - 【15†read here†tsx.hirok.io】
L64:   * node-postgres - package for querying your PostgreSQL database - 【16†read here†node-postgres.com】
L65: 
L66: Drizzle has native support for PostgreSQL connections with the `node-postgres` and `postgres.js` drivers.
L67: We will use `node-postgres` for this get started example. But if you want to find more ways to connect to postgresql check our 【17†PostgreSQL Connection】 page
L68: #### Basic [REDACTED] structure
L69: 
L70: This is the basic [REDACTED] structure of the project. In the `src/db` directory, we have table definition in `schema.ts`. In `drizzle` folder there are sql migration file and snapshots.
L71: 
L72:     `📦 <project root>
L73:      ├ 📂 drizzle
L74:      ├ 📂 src
L75:      │   ├ 📂 db
L76:      │   │  └ 📜 schema.ts
L77:      │   └ 📜 index.ts
L78:      ├ 📜 .env
L79:      ├ 📜 drizzle.config.ts
L80:      ├ 📜 package.json
L81:      └ 📜 tsconfig.json`
L82: #### Step 1 - Install node-postgres package
L83: 
L84: npm
L85: 
L86: yarn
L87: 
L88: pnpm
L89: 
L90: bun
L91: 
L92:     `npm i drizzle-orm@rc pg dotenv
L93:     npm i -D drizzle-kit@rc tsx @types/pg`
L94: 
L95:     `yarn add drizzle-orm@rc pg dotenv
L96:     yarn add -D drizzle-kit@rc tsx @types/pg`
L97: 
L98:     `pnpm add drizzle-orm@rc pg dotenv
L99:     pnpm add -D drizzle-kit@rc tsx @types/pg`
L100: 
L101:     `bun add drizzle-orm@rc pg dotenv
L102:     bun add -D drizzle-kit@rc tsx @types/pg`
L103: #### Step 2 - Setup connection variables
L104: 
L105: Create a `.env` file in the root of your project and add your database connection variable:
L106: 
L107:     `DATABASE_URL=`
L108: 
L109: tips
L110: 
L111: If you don’t have a PostgreSQL database yet and want to create one for testing, you can use our guide on how to set up PostgreSQL in Docker.
L112: 
L113: The PostgreSQL in Docker guide is available 【18†here】. Go set it up, generate a database URL (explained in the guide), and come back for the next steps
L114: #### Step 3 - Connect Drizzle ORM to the database
L115:

L124:     import { drizzle } from 'drizzle-orm/node-postgres';
L125: 
L126:     const db = drizzle(process.env.DATABASE_URL!);`
L127: 
L128:     `import 'dotenv/config';
L129:     import { drizzle } from 'drizzle-orm/node-postgres';
L130: 
L131:     // You can specify any property from the node-postgres connection options
L132:     const db = drizzle({
L133:       connection: {
L134:         connectionString: process.env.DATABASE_URL!,
L135:         ssl: true
L136:       }
L137:     });`
L138:     `import 'dotenv/config';
L139:     import { drizzle } from "drizzle-orm/node-postgres";

L141: 
L142:     const pool = new Pool({
L143:       connectionString: process.env.DATABASE_URL!,
L144:     });
L145:     const db = drizzle({ client: pool });`
L146: #### Step 4 - Create a table

L156:       name: varchar({ length: 255 }).notNull(),
L157:       age: integer().notNull(),
L158:       email: varchar({ length: 255 }).notNull().unique(),
L159:     });`
